answer: Bonded reputation resists sybils in an agent economy: every identity locks a bond before trading, and peer attestation is weighted by verified history, not one-vote-per-key. Honest agents are a grove — trust grows like roots between real trees, while a sybil forest planted overnight has no depth. The bond is the costly pigment on each identity: an attacker pays genuine capital per fake agent and faces slashing when peers catch fabrication. History-weighted influence means a thousand fakes weigh no more than a few genuine agents — a ferrous law, hard to forge and unyielding to cheaters.
